prompt: Which query does Testing Library put first in its order of preference?

choices.text: getByTestId
choices.why: It is the last resort: no person sees a test id.

choices.text: getByText
choices.why: Fourth, for what is not interactive.

choices.text: getByRole
choices.why: Right. Role and accessible name, as assistive technology reads them.

choices.text: getByPlaceholderText
choices.why: Third, and a field that needs it has a problem.

prompt: You rename the class `.tick` to `.done-button`. Which test still passes?

choices.text: One that finds the button with `querySelector(".tick")`
choices.why: The selector no longer matches anything.

choices.text: One that asks for the button named Done
choices.why: Right. Nothing a person sees changed.

choices.text: Neither, because both read the DOM
choices.why: Both read it; only one depends on the class.

choices.text: Both, because jsdom ignores classes
choices.why: jsdom keeps classes exactly as written.

prompt: Why does a test that cannot find a control by its name point at an accessibility problem?

choices.why: It runs no screen reader; it reads the same structure one would.

choices.why: Right. No name for the test means no name for the person.

choices.text: Because WCAG requires every page to be tested with Testing Library
choices.why: WCAG names no tool.

choices.text: It does not; the two are unrelated
choices.why: They are related, and this lesson's red test is the proof.

prompt: Why can the planner use `@testing-library/dom` without any framework?

choices.text: It works on any DOM

choices.text: It bundles its own copy of React
choices.why: It bundles no framework.

choices.text: Vite turns plain TypeScript into components for it
choices.why: Vite does nothing of the kind.

choices.text: It only reads HTML files from disk
choices.why: It reads the live document.

prompt: To add the jest-dom matchers to the `expect` of the runner this course uses, a test file imports `@testing-library/jest-dom/___`.

choices.text: Because `markDone` was removed

choices.text: A click cannot be recorded in jsdom

choices.text: The page itself is the output

prompt: What does `within(screen.getByRole("list"))` do?

choices.text: Waits until the list appears

choices.text: Limits the next queries to the list

choices.text: Copies the list into a new document

choices.text: Counts the items of the list

choices.text: somebody interrupted halfway through the form

choices.text: somebody using a screen reader

choices.text: somebody with low vision

choices.text: A way past `addSession`'s check

prompt: Why must every `user.…` call be awaited?

choices.text: Because user-event downloads a browser
choices.why: It downloads nothing.

choices.text: Or the test reads the page too soon
choices.why: Right. It passes or fails by timing.

choices.text: TypeScript refuses an unawaited promise
choices.why: It allows one; that is the danger.

choices.text: Vitest only counts awaited tests
choices.why: It counts every test.

prompt: Put the events `user.type(field, "1")` produces in order.
Why did the fetch move out of `main.ts` into `start()` in `app.ts`?

choices.text: Vite cannot serve a module that uses await at its top level
choices.why: It served it in lesson 1.

choices.text: Because `fetch` does not exist in the browser
choices.why: It does; the page still uses it.

choices.text: Importing `main.ts` runs it; a test calls `start()` instead
choices.why: Right. The behaviour did not change; its reach did.

choices.text: To make the page load faster
choices.why: Speed did not change.

prompt: `start(root, load)` takes `load` as a parameter with `fetch` as its default. What does the test gain over replacing the global `fetch`?

choices.text: Nothing; the two are the same thing
choices.why: One touches a global every other test shares.

choices.text: Speed, since parameters are faster than globals
choices.why: The difference is not speed.

choices.text: Type safety, since `fetch` has no types
choices.why: `fetch` is fully typed.

choices.text: No global is replaced, so nothing leaks into other tests
choices.why: Right. The test passes what it needs and leaves the rest alone.

prompt: Match each thing to find with the query that fits it best.
Which assertion checks that the Done button has gone?

choices.text: `expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Done" })).not.toBeInTheDocument()`
choices.why: `getBy…` throws before the assertion runs.

choices.text: `expect(screen.queryByRole("button", { name: "Done" })).not.toBeInTheDocument()`
choices.why: Right. `queryBy…` returns null.

choices.text: `await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Done" })`
choices.why: That waits for it to appear.

choices.text: `expect(screen.getAllByRole("button")).toHaveLength(0)`
choices.why: Add session is still a button, and `getAll…` throws on none.
